title: Octave Web signs in through the household's provider by a one-time code only its own tab can redeem
description: Octave Web, jellyscale's browser client (D-089), needs single sign-on without a cookie (#296).
notes: Waits for an Octave Web build that starts the sign-in, as JS-150 waits for one (D-099). Dropped (D-126 and the pivot, D-107): Merged into JS-039, single sign-on for Octave on every platform.
acceptanceCriteria: The provider's tokens never reach the page. The return carries only a one-time code that expires in about 60 seconds. The code is redeemed once, by the verifier of the tab that started the sign-in, and a second redemption or a wrong verifier is refused.
No route reads or sets a cookie (invariant 63). The journey is over HTTPS only. With real processes, start, return and redemption are each answered by a different api replica.
A threat review of the handoff is recorded before Build. Its guessing bound follows JS-039's.
Octave Web, as built, signs in through the provider and plays. The device holds an ordinary token, as JS-039's criterion 2 describes.
